subject: Discovery recap: p95 latency targets, streaming UX & concurrency requirements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michael Thompson <michael.thompson@finly.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@finly.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: p95 latency targets, streaming UX & concurrency requirements

Hi Michael / Priya —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. If I missed anything, please correct.

Pain points you called out:
- Chat streaming feels laggy for users; target UX is near-instant token streaming for first tokens (perceived latency).
- Current p95 generation latency spikes to ~650ms for 512-token contexts on your prod model variant during peak traffic.
- Concurrency requirement: need to sustain ~120–150 concurrent streaming sessions with headroom for bursts to 250.
- Occasional CPU/memory pressure on the API proxies when KV cache misses happen.

Current stack (what you shared):
- Frontend: React streaming client using SSE
- Inference: self-hosted model on GCP custom VMs (NVIDIA A10s) via an internal inference service
- Autoscaling via Kubernetes HPA + custom queueing at the proxy layer

Success criteria for a POC we agreed on:
- p95 end-to-end streaming latency <= 200ms for first N tokens under steady-state load (120 concurrency)
- Sustained throughput at target concurrency with <5% error rate and no degraded UX (no stalled streams)
- Clear remediation plan for cold-starts and KV cache warm-up to avoid first-request penalties

Proposed next steps / owners:
- Finly: share a 24–72h anonymized telemetry snapshot and example prompt workload (Michael / Priya). [Attachment request below]
- Redwood (Aditya): run an initial profiling pass on that workload and propose a target config (batching, token beam, quantization tradeoffs).
- Redwood (Marissa): prepare an initial cost/throughput estimate and schedule a 2-hour perf test window next week.

Attachments referenced: [Attachment: finly-telemetry-snapshot.pdf (PDF, 420KB)], [Attachment: finly-current-arch.png (PNG, 220KB)].

I’ll follow up with available slots for the perf test. Thanks again — this looks like a great fit to validate with a short PoC.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Michael Thompson <michael.thompson@finly.com>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 16:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: p95 latency targets, streaming UX & concurrency requirements

Marissa — thanks for the write-up; that matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 650ms p95 number is for our "prod-v1" model. We also have a smaller "prod-v1-small" variant used for web fallback that averages ~320ms p95 but has lower quality on long-form replies.
- Our streaming client uses an SSE-based polyfill; some clients are on mobile where network jitter amplifies the perceived lag. Improving the first-token arrival matters a lot.
- We can share telemetry (anonymized traces and 24h request samples) by EOD. I’ve attached an excerpt.

Agree to the POC success criteria. For scheduling, next Tuesday or Wednesday AM PST works — we prefer earlier times.

Michael
Michael Thompson
Head of Product, Finly
michael.thompson@finly.com
[Attachment: finly-telemetry-snapshot.pdf (excerpt)]
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michael Thompson <michael.thompson@finly.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 16:50:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: p95 latency targets, streaming UX & concurrency requirements

Thanks Michael — that excerpt helps. A few quick technical notes / questions so we scope the perf test correctly: 

- Can you confirm the average and tail token lengths for interactive sessions (we need to know typical context lengths — e.g., 128 vs 512 tokens).
- Do you have a cached KV-store pattern today or is KV always rebuilt per session? If there’s an opportunity to warm KV or persist prefixes we can reduce p95 significantly.
- Which model families are you running? If you can run the smaller variant in parity with the same tokenizer and prompt engineering, we can measure delta in latency vs. quality.

Proposed test plan (high level):
1) Baseline: replay 5–10m of real traffic at low load to capture warm/warmless differences.
2) Steady-state: ramp to 120 concurrent streaming sessions for 15m and measure p50/p95/p99 for first-token and overall generation.
3) Burst test: spike to 250 concurrency for 3–5m to observe autoscaling and failure modes.
4) Streaming UX validation: measure first-token arrival times at the client (SSE) under simulated jitter.

We’ll prepare a perf harness based on your telemetry. If possible, include a small sample of representative prompts (5–10) that drive long-form generation. We can run the initial profiling on our sandbox GPUs and share the profiling output + recommended config (batch size, tokenization/windowing, recommended kernel/quantization).

Ethan — we’ll want to start with a 2x warm replica count and enable prefix caching for the test. Can you confirm availability to support the window next Tue/Wed AM PST?

—Aditya
Aditya Rao | Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: p95 latency targets, streaming UX & concurrency requirements

Thanks all — good questions and good plan.

Michael / Priya: if you can drop the 24h telemetry + 5–10 representative prompts into the Drive folder (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Finly-POC) I’ll kick off the profiling and lock in a perf window for Tue 12/8 9:00–11:00 AM PST (tentative).

Quick replies inline:
> Can you confirm the average and tail token lengths for interactive sessions?
We expect ~128 avg, 512 tail for ~10% of sessions — Michael to confirm exact percentiles after sending the telemetry.

> Do you have a cached KV-store pattern today?
Not persistently; proxy builds KV per session today — Aditya will prototype prefix caching during the PoC.

Aditya / Ethan: please confirm availability and I’ll send a calendar invite + test plan doc (will include estimated-costs.xlsx).

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to the POC.

Best,
Marissa
